### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 34 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a21fd6c531e50a53deb26a7d04886fbb073164e8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5c3541906c2ff3af0ef879f59bb8db852058d65f` — the merge of head `cb986e3825c8b44abe0f1e148cb6b114439a0f2d` into base `a21fd6c531e50a53deb26a7d04886fbb073164e8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5c3541906c2ff3af0ef879f59bb8db852058d65f && git checkout 5c3541906c2ff3af0ef879f59bb8db852058d65f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a21fd6c531e50a53deb26a7d04886fbb073164e8 cb986e3825c8b44abe0f1e148cb6b114439a0f2d && git checkout -B drift-repro a21fd6c531e50a53deb26a7d04886fbb073164e8 && git merge --no-ff cb986e3825c8b44abe0f1e148cb6b114439a0f2d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a21fd6c531e50a53deb26a7d04886fbb073164e8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a21fd6c531e50a53deb26a7d04886fbb073164e8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cb986e3825c8b44abe0f1e148cb6b114439a0f2d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-extension-system-columns.test.ts, packages/plugins/organizations/src/object-extension-managed-target.wall.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-extension-agreement.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-overlay-extension-fold.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-object-extension-meta-read.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`), packages/metadata-core/src/audit-field-governance.ts (`applyAuditFieldGovernance`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts (`authObjectExtensions`), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts (`lock` docblock), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`getMetaItemLayered`, `foldObjectExtendersFromRegistry`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (#21613 `withDeclaredColumnsOnly` / `declaredColumnSet`), packages/objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts (`resolveTenantFieldName`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts and security-plugin.ts (`tenancyDisabled`), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts (orphaned-column pass), packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts (`findV17ShapeTables`), packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts and organization-ownership-plan.ts (D10 fates), .github/workflows/ci.yml (the dogfood job's `if:`), and the prose face .changeset/24314-extension-no-injected-columns.md under ②. Base `e4bcced0b451` (merge-base of `origin/main` and the head); 8 commits on the head, 7 commits of `origin/main` (`a2a3777bf5` at review time) not on it, `git merge-tree --write-tree` clean.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Which contributors are planned — RIGHT.** `registerObject` now runs `applySystemFields` only when `ownership !== 'extend'` (registry.ts:3103), so an `own` or `overlay` body is planned at its own registration and an `extend` body is stored as the author wrote it (the new unit pin's contributor-only case reads the stored layer and finds only `summary`). The fold (`foldExtendersOntoDefinition`) spreads the raw extension fields over the planned base; `resolveObject` takes `overlay ?? own` as base and `resolveOwnerLayer` takes `own`, both planned. Order-independence holds by construction: planning is a per-base act at that base's registration and the fold happens at resolve, so an extender registered before its owner is held raw until the owner arrives planned. The unit pin covers six target shapes in both orders, asserting field-for-field equality with the unextended control plus exactly `summary`, and `indexes` equality. One further derived change the diff does not name: an ordinary multi-tenant extended object no longer carries a second copy of the platform's tenant index entry (`mergeObjectDefinitions` concatenates `indexes`, `resolveObject` subtracts nothing, and the planned extension body used to contribute its own `{ fields: ['organization_id'] }`); the pin's `indexes` equality would not have held before.

2. **Target shapes that lose a column — each equals the target's own declaration — RIGHT.** By the plan table in `injected-system-columns.ts`: `managedBy: 'better-auth'` and `systemFields: false` lose `organization_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` (and on a non-`sys_` name `owner_id`, `owning_business_unit_id`) because rows 1-2 plan nothing; `tenancy.enabled: false` loses `organization_id`; `ownership` other than `user` loses the ownership anchors; a platform-global deployment object loses `organization_id` (`setDeploymentPlatformGlobalObjects` now `continue`s on an `extend` layer after the authored-column check, so an extension's own authored `organization_id` is still reported in `keptAuthoredColumn`). An authored `organization_id` on the owner is not a loss but a restore: the extension body's injected `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` (a readonly lookup) used to win the field spread over the author's column; now the author's stands. No target that should keep a column loses it: an ordinary extended object keeps the owner's full plan (pin row 6); an overlay base is planned at registration (`ownership === 'overlay'` passes `applySystemFields`) and extenders fold onto it; an owner registered after its extender is planned when it arrives. The registered set, the served set (`getObject` and every `/meta` exit that folds through `foldObjectExtendersOnto`) and the stored set (the driver's `syncSchema` reads the registered schema) move together; the accept set of the extension door (`ObjectExtensionSchema`, untouched) does not move.

3. **The audit-governance fold — RIGHT, with one named edge.** `governAudit = resolveInjectedSystemColumns(baseDefinition).audit`; when true, `applyAuditFieldGovernance(contrib.definition)` forces `AUDIT_FIELD_GOVERNANCE` (`readonly: true`, `system: true`) onto every audit-provenance field the extension DECLARES and touches nothing absent (audit-field-governance.ts:121-148). That is the same key set `applySystemFields`' `overrides` branch forced on the planned extension body, so #4447's protection is kept for every target that carries the audit family (ordinary objects, every non-better-auth `managedBy` bucket, an overlay base), and the pin's `TARGETS[5]` case shows the extension's label kept and `readonly: true` forced. Without this fold the fix would have regressed #4447, because `mergeObjectDefinitions` lets the extension's field win the spread. For a target whose plan carries no audit family (`managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `systemFields: false`, `systemFields.audit: false`) the fold applies nothing, and an extension-declared audit-named field stands as written — the pin's better-auth case asserts `readonly: false`. This differs from before (planning the bare body governed it on every target) and is parity with what the owner's own declaration already gets there: `applySystemFields` returns before governance on rows 1-2 and when `systemFields.audit === false`, and `applyAuditFieldGovernance`'s own doc says opt-out objects "carry no platform governance and are returned untouched". #4447's stated protection ("a declared `created_at` cannot make the AUDIT ANCHOR client-writable") has no anchor on such a target. Judged right; carried into ② as the one write-door relaxation.

4. **plugin-auth's `sys_sso_provider` — RIGHT, nothing depends on what is removed.** Declaration: `managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `tenancy: { enabled: false }`, `lock: 'full'`, `organization_id: Field.text({ maxLength: 255 })`, `created_at`/`updated_at` declared readonly, indexes on `provider_id`, `domain`, `user_id`, `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']`. The extension (`authObjectExtensions`, manifest.ts:109) adds `oidc_client_secret`. Before: the bare body planned `organization_id` (lookup, readonly), `created_by`, `updated_by`, and `provisionTenantScopeIndex` appended the tenant index; the field spread replaced the authored text column with the lookup. After: the declaration stands. Readers: no plugin-auth source reads `created_by`, `updated_by` or `organization_id` on this object (grep over `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src`, non-test); better-auth's SSO adapter writes its own provider-to-organization relation into the text column. The wall: `tenancy.enabled: false` makes `tenancyDisabled` true and `computeTenantLayer0Filter` return `LAYER0_NONE` (tenant-layer.ts:134), and `resolveTenantFieldName` returns null on `tenancy.enabled === false` (system-write-organization.ts:211), so neither the lookup type nor the index was load-bearing. The D10 inventory row for `sys_sso_provider` ('report', `notNullExempt`, "tenancy.enabled: false on a declared organization_id") already describes the post-fix declared state.

5. **Existing databases with stray injected columns — nothing fails, warns or serves them wrongly — RIGHT; not a card.** Schema sync only adds (boot-guard docblock). The engine's #21613 narrowing (`withDeclaredColumnsOnly(…, declaredColumnSet(registry.getObject(object)))`) shapes every served, returned and pre-image row to the declared set, so an undeclared `organization_id`/`created_by`/`updated_by` is never served and never recorded as a change. The drift pass (schema-drift.ts:1396-1415) REPORTS such a column as `unmapped_column` ("column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned)") with an opt-in destructive `drop_column` op — a report, not a failure. The v18 boot guard (`findV17ShapeTables`) judges only objects declaring `systemFields.tenant: false`, so a better-auth table is never refused. The D10 ceremony lists `sys_organization` and `sys_user` as `noColumn` → fate `column-drop`, and its plan drops a PRESENT `organization_id` ("the column is dropped (fate 1)"), so the stray tenant column already has a fate on the upgrade path; `created_by`/`updated_by` stay orphaned and drift-reported. The PR's acceptance note is accurate; it could add that the drift report lists them.

6. **The three flipped pins — re-aimed to the truth; two of three load-bearing for this defect, the third load-bearing for its own.** `getMetaItemLayered` leaves `code` and `overlay` RAW and governs only `effective` (`governServedObject(effectiveBase)`; protocol.ts: "`code` and `overlay` are deliberately left RAW"), and `code` is `foldObjectExtendersFromRegistry(serviceBody)` — the artifact's owner body plus the extension fields. The old `code == listed` held only because the planned extension body grafted the platform columns into `code`. (a) rest `meta-object-extension-agreement`: `code` now equals `Object.keys(OWNER_DECLARATION.fields) + EXTENSION_FIELDS`; under the mutation the grafted columns return and the pin reds — load-bearing. (b) rest `meta-object-overlay-extension-fold`: compares `declaredFieldsOf` (platform columns filtered) on both layers, the comparison every other case in that file uses; its own defect (#8027: `effective` lacking the extension fields in one response) is still caught; it is no longer sensitive to #24314 by construction, and did not need to be. (c) dogfood `showcase-object-extension-meta-read`: `code` equals the showcase's own `showcase_account` declaration (objectstack.config.ts `objects: [...Object.values(objects), …]`; account.object.ts declares no audit, owner or tenant column; the lowering `normalizeStackInput → lowerCallables → ObjectStackDefinitionSchema → JSON.stringify` adds no field and `ObjectSchema` has no field-adding transform) plus `EXTENSION_FIELDS`, `effective` still equals the list read, `overlay` stays null — load-bearing by the same reading as (a). ⚠ No check-run on this head executed it: `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3..3/3)` and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are `skipped` because the job's `if:` excludes `pull_request` and `merge_group` (ci.yml:2026); the aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green by attestation count over a skipped matrix. The dogfood pin's only execution is the dev's local run (20 passed, a claim). It runs on the push to `main` after landing.

7. **The booted walled pin — proves what the card asks, with a real control — RIGHT.** `bootStack` + this package's `OrganizationsPlugin`, `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`, `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only`; the owner is a signed-up user who created the organisation (not the platform owner), the member is invited, accepted and set-active. It asserts the registered schema and the physical table (`PRAGMA table_info`) carry the extension field and none of the five withheld columns, for `sys_organization` and `sys_user`; owner and member read the organisation by list and by id (200, the org id present); each reads their own user row by id and the member sees it in the `sys_user` list; control: the member's read of the platform owner's organisation is `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` and that id is absent from the list. The control is real for the organisation wall. No cross-organisation control exists for `sys_user`; the card did not ask one and `sys_user` never carried the tenant column before the extension, so the pin restores the control state rather than widening it. Wall time is unmeasured here (a booted file with a 120 s `beforeAll`); the 10 s ruling makes an over-budget file its lane's card, report-only, and the three sibling `bootStack` tests in the package declare no budget either.

8. **The `epic:#15194` lane — no collision, aligned direction.** The PR's one source path is `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`. #15194's declared C8 territory is `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (tenant derivation, system-insert stamping), `packages/objectql/src/tenancy/platform-object-tenancy.ts`, `plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts`, the driver's `applyTenantScope`, `scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` and the named NULL-organization readings; none is touched, and `platform-object-tenancy.ts` is a ledger the registry's plan does not feed. ADR-0131 D1 ("NULL is not a state"): the change removes an `organization_id` that was NULL on every row of a better-auth table, and the stray column on upgraded databases is D10 fate 1 — in the ADR's direction. No comment on #15194 is owed.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/24314-extension-no-injected-columns.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, marked **BREAKING** (a served-set narrowing) and "shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention" — matches `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header ("During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`"). The PR title carries `!`. Only `@objectstack/objectql` source changes; the rest and dogfood edits are test files and owe no changeset. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — truthful: no stored metadata changes shape, no spec key, export or error code is added or removed (`injected-system-columns.ts`, `packages/platform-objects` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` are untouched; the one new import is of an already-exported `@objectstack/metadata-core` symbol), and the body carries no FROM → TO rewrite ("nothing to rewrite"; the "read the owner's own columns" sentence names a column the object never declared). The gate's precondition for the category (refused when the body carries a migration prescription) holds and the gate is green.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body (the seat's re-declaration) and at the changeset's line head — **truthful for the inherit route.** The extension door accepts the same bodies; the public surface of `@objectstack/objectql` is unchanged; the served and stored sets narrow (an extended opt-out target loses columns its declaration withholds; `sys_sso_provider`'s `organization_id` reverts to the declared text and loses `created_by`, `updated_by` and the tenant index). One write-door corner is honoured where it used to be refused: a PATCH of an audit-named field that an EXTENSION declared on a target whose plan carries no audit family (`managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `systemFields: false`, `systemFields.audit: false`) is no longer stripped as readonly (① item 3; pinned). That is a `no` of the kind execution-duties names — removing a refusal the published contract text already negates — and the text is: `injected-system-columns.ts` plan rows 1-2 ("nothing"), `applySystemFields`' early return on those rows and on `systemFields.audit === false`, and `applyAuditFieldGovernance`'s doc ("Objects that opt out of the audit family … carry no platform governance and are returned untouched — the same rows `applySystemFields` skips"). The platform governs nothing on such a target, the column is the extension's own, and the owner's declaration was already accepted there, so no PUBLISHED accept set widens. The PR body's line does not cite this text; see ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Route INHERIT, not the hypothesised refusal (open_questions[0]) — answered: A, confirmed.** The defect is the plan computed on the wrong body and reaches every opt-out row; a refusal of `lock: 'full'` targets covers two rows, needs an owner exemption for plugin-auth's same-package extension (which was measured defective) and two order-dependent refusal sites. The inherit route has no exemption and no tolerance branch. `H1`'s premise that better-auth's "extra columns would collide" covers an extension's own fields was measured false on the walled boot (sign-up, create, invite, accept, set-active ran with them). C is not needed.
- **Three test-only edits outside the claim's file list — answered: accepted.** Each pinned the raw `code` layer equal to the governed list read, an equality that held only through the defect; made under the pin-sweep instruction; test files publish nothing; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is green.
- **The audit-governance fold beyond the one guard — answered: necessary and correct** (① item 3). Pinned and, per the report, ablated red 1 of 14; the reading agrees: without it `mergeObjectDefinitions` lets a writable extension `created_at` win over the base's readonly definition.
- **os-dev vs dispatch on merging `origin/main` last — answered: the dev was right to follow os-dev.md** (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:279`: after the PR opens, main is merged only on a conflict, a main-caused red or a dequeue; `:188-189`: the agent file wins and the conflict is named in the report, which it was). The head is 7 commits behind `origin/main` with a clean `merge-tree`; the merge group rebuilds against `main`, so nothing is owed.
- **Shallow-clone deepening** (`git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-13` for two history gates) — benign; AGENTS.md's rule is answer-or-refuse on windowed history and the gates answered after the fetch.
- **open_questions[1], the `protection.lock` docblock — escalated: it IS a card, `domain:spec`, docs-only, route A.** The `lock` docblock (protection.zod.ts) says `no-overlay` "is recommended for … core objects whose fields can be extended via `objectExtensions`" and `full` "is for items that have no safe extension point at all"; the semantics table governs Save and Delete only, no door enforces the sentence at registration, and the platform's own practice contradicts it (`sys_sso_provider`, `sys_user`, `sys_organization` are `full` and extended; after this PR extending them is safe). Published spec text that misleads an author about what the lock does is a metadata-authoring trap under Prime Directive #10: reword, do not enforce — the measured need for B is absent (every existing extension is legitimate). Not blocking this PR; the seat files it.
- **open_questions[2], the Clause-② line — answered: A, keep `no (narrowing)`, and the seat should mirror the citation.** The record's ② carries the contract text that negates the one withdrawn refusal; the PR body's parenthetical names only the served-set narrowing. Append the citation when the body is next touched so the `no` reads complete on the carrier the gate reads.
- **open_questions[3], the PR-body amendment — answered: done.** Verified on the body at review time: the Clause-② parenthetical names the inherit route, the audit-governance paragraph sits under "What changed", the verification record names `cb986e382` and 8305. The rest and plugin-auth suite lines still name no head (measured at `8316f5b58` per the report); immaterial — Test Core on the head is the verdict.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0], stray columns on existing databases — judged: not a card** (① item 5): `organization_id` is D10 fate 1 on the upgrade path, `created_by`/`updated_by` are orphans the drift report lists with an opt-in drop, the boot guard does not judge better-auth tables, and the engine never serves an undeclared column. An acceptance-note sentence naming the drift report would complete the note.
- **out_of_scope_findings[1], the lock docblock — judged: a card** (above).
- **Check-runs on the head: 48 read, none failed, none in progress.** Success: Test Core (6/6 shards and aggregate), Build Core, TypeScript Type Check and its four jobs, Lint & Repo Gates and its eight jobs, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset (both events), Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Spec property liveness, the three claim/card checks (both events), filter, Auto Label. Skipped by path or event: Dogfood Regression Gate shards 1-3 and Dogfood Verify CLI (pull_request excluded by the job's `if:`), Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, and Check PR Size / Auto Label on the second (edited) event. The dogfood pin is therefore unexecuted by CI until the push to `main`; the seat watches that run.
- **Independence:** the diff was produced on the branch by the dev session named in the dispatch (`session_01GJL9Zar94zzHuG5XV78dUM`); this record is rendered for the dispatching seat, which adopts it.

## 席位核对 · `domain:engine` seat 1 · `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy` · 2026-10-18T17:00Z · **ACCEPT**

Head: `cb986e382` (the fix, a merge of `main`, the audit-governance fold and a changeset note). Card #24314, claim 6250813213, dispatch 6250833640. Dev report: 6252287854.

| Item | Reading |
| --- | --- |
| Shape | Draft PR → `main`. The body opens `Fixes #24314`. 7 files, +384 / −17. Not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 24363`: 0 of 7 paths; 401 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold). |
| Scope | One source file, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`. Two new pins, one unit and one on a booted walled kernel. Three re-aimed pins (`packages/rest` x2, `packages/qa/dogfood`), test-only, outside the claim's list, made under the pin-sweep instruction. These are declared to `domain:cli` (6252426269, 6252431657) and to `domain:services` for the `organizations` wall test (6252437883). One changeset for `@objectstack/objectql`. `injected-system-columns.ts`, `packages/platform-objects` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` are untouched; there is no new error code and no migration. |
| Seat's own read | At the head: `registerObject` plans a contributor only when `ownership !== 'extend'`. `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` applies `applyAuditFieldGovernance` to an extender only when the base plan carries the audit family. `setDeploymentPlatformGlobalObjects` skips an `extend` layer after its authored-column check. `applyAuditFieldGovernance`'s doc says opt-out objects "carry no platform governance". The dogfood job's `if:` excludes `pull_request` and `merge_group`. |
| Route | **Inherit**, not the claim's provisional refusal. The defect is the plan computed on the wrong body, and it reaches every opt-out target shape.
